messages:
Sam Carter: Quick spike — we need a very tight two-slide bench narrative that connects response time to product economics. Can we sketch the hooks?
Maya Singh: love it. aim for one visual that non-ML folks grok in 5s, one detailed callout for engineers.
Elaine Park: agree. top-line: 'Faster median responses -> fewer GPU-seconds per session' then a secondary axis for $/1000 sessions.
Devon Liu: for visuals: scatter of latency percentile vs $/k requests, color by model family. call out the knee where batching or KV cache saves most.
Axel Gomez: incoming leads care about two things: predictable bill + latency SLOs. slide 1 = story + simple chart. slide 2 = operational levers (batching, quantization, routing policies) with one-line cost impact each.
Maya Singh: copy idea: headline = "Response time is a product lever, not a mystery" subhead = "Optimize latency to reduce per-session compute and increase efficiency"
Sam Carter: good. can we show an example: e.g., p50=120ms -> $0.08/session, p50=300ms -> $0.14/session (ballpark). callout: caching and prefix sharing reduce tokens by ~x%.
Devon Liu: can put a tiny table/code block with how we measured:
```
model: open-7B
seq: 512
workload: chat-like (avg 4 turns)
measure: 1M requests across 3 regions
metric: median latency, p95, tokens per session, $/session (est)
```
Elaine Park: we should avoid overselling numbers. use ranges and say "example workload". and include a small footnote about pricing assumptions.
Sam Carter: agree. Maya — can you draft the two slides? Axel — routing + demo CTA to propose for webinar registration flow.
Maya Singh: will draft by EOD. I'll mock the chart in Figma, include annotations for the knee, a 3-segment legend (small, medium, large workload slices).
Axel Gomez: for inbound routing: add a tracking param to the webinar CTA so sales gets workload type. e.g., `?src=bench_p50_small` so leads flagged for "cost-sensitive" vs "latency-first".
Devon Liu: also add a checklist for engineering QAs in slide notes: reproducibility script, dataset slice definitions, quant settings. short bullets only.
marketing-bot: Reminder: Upcoming webinar slot on 2026-04-07 10:00 PT. Capacity: 200 live seats.
Elaine Park: perfect — that date works for the case study customers we want to invite.
Sam Carter: ok next steps: Maya drafts slides + one-line social post. Devon produces a 100-line reproducibility gist (link to be added). Axel wires CTA with tracking. We'll sync tomorrow morning for copy polish. :thumbsup:
